learningObjective: Understand what the texture / read-only cache path provides and when it is beneficial.

hardwareContext.architecture: Kepler and newer (Kepler introduced read-only path; texture cache older)
requiredFeatures: read-only cache / __ldg intrinsic; texture object API

stem: Which statement about the CUDA texture / read-only cache path (accessed via `__ldg`, texture objects, or `__restrict__` const pointers) is correct?

options.text: The read-only path routes global-memory loads through a separate cache (historically the texture cache) that is optimized for read-only, spatially-local data; it can improve L1 pressure and bandwidth for read-only inputs (e.g., weight matrices), and is triggered by `__ldg` or by loading through `const T* __restrict__` pointers on Kepler and later.
The texture cache is faster than shared memory for all access patterns; users should therefore always convert `__shared__` allocations to texture-bound arrays for peak performance.
`__ldg` is a synchronous host-side intrinsic that pre-copies data from device global memory to host DRAM; using it inside a kernel produces undefined behavior.
The read-only path bypasses coherence; using it on data that another kernel wrote in the same stream will always return stale values, so it should only be used for compile-time-constant arrays.

explanation: The read-only data path routes loads through a cache designed for read-only access (historically shared with the texture unit; on modern GPUs unified with L1 to varying degrees). It reduces pressure on the main L1 for read-only inputs and is triggered explicitly by `__ldg(ptr)` or implicitly when the compiler proves a pointer is read-only (e.g., `const T* __restrict__`). It is beneficial for weights and other broadcast/spatially-local reads. Choice B overstates: the texture cache is not universally faster than SMEM. Choice C confuses `__ldg` with a host API. Choice D wrongly claims coherence problems within the standard CUDA memory model.

optionExplanations.A: Correct: read-only path via `__ldg` / `const __restrict__` on Kepler+.
optionExplanations.B: Wrong: SMEM is a distinct, generally faster on-chip memory.
optionExplanations.D: Wrong: no stale-value coherence issue within a stream.

nonImplications: Does not imply the read-only path is always faster; for write-heavy or streaming data, L1/L2 paths are appropriate.
Does not imply texture objects and __ldg are equivalent; texture objects also offer addressing modes and normalization.

distractorRationales.C: Confuses device intrinsic with host API.
